v.why: Large batches give few updates in 243 epochs, so a bigger Adam step compensates for step starvation.
Larger batches average out gradient noise, which tames instability at very high learning rates.
Narrow nets have little spare capacity, so more L2 pushes them into underfitting.
The L2 penalty is scaled per batch, so small batches feel a stronger effective penalty and extra alpha over-regularizes.
Wider layers make each of the few large-batch updates more productive, offsetting step starvation.
Wider nets change their output faster per step at a small learning rate, compensating for slow progress.
Under Adam, wider layers amplify the effect of each large step, so large rates become more unstable.
Deeper ReLU nets compound large updates across layers and diverge or die more easily at high rates.
Smaller batches multiply the per-sample L2 strength, pushing an already strong penalty into underfitting.
L2 shrinkage compounds across layers, so strong alpha collapses the signal further in deeper nets.
